subject: How to denote columns in a data frame

messages.author: decd30055c435d87
messages.subject: How to denote columns in a data frame
parts:
Hello ggplotters, This may be a general R problem, but I have only
encountered it with ggplot. I have this code, which works fine:

ggplot(data=summative.plus.read2, aes(x=as.factor(rating.1),
y=standard_va))+geom_boxplot()

(rating.1 has integer values 1:4, and standard_va is continuous)

However I have 8 columns in the data frame that I want similar boxplots
for, named like this:
comp.columns <- paste("rating.", c(1:4, 6:9), sep='')

I tried putting this in a loop like so:

for(i in 1:8) {
ggplot(data=summative.plus.read2, aes(x=as.factor(comp.columns[i]),
y=standard_va))+geom_boxplot()
}

but all I get is one boxplot, while all the ratings.n columns have 4
levels, so I'm expecting one boxplot for each of the 4 levels. I tried
using many different combinations of eval, substitute, deparse, etc. on
this but didn't have any success. Can someone give me a clue?

TIA

messages.subject: Re: How to denote columns in a data frame
parts:
Hi,

I think you should use facetting; first, you need to reshape your data
in long format,

library(reshape2)
m = melt(summative.plus.read2, id = "standard_va", meas =
paste0("rating.", c(1:4, 6:9)))

str(m)

## now plot with facets
ggplot(data=m, aes(x=value, y=standard_va)) +
facet_wrap( ~ variable ) +
geom_boxplot()

(written in the dark)

HTH,

b.
